articles.title: Fantasy Basketball Waiver Wire: The Playlist for your Week 3 lineup
articles.summary: Dan Titus breaks down the top fantasy hoops adds of the week, plus schedule advice to help you navigate your matchups.
articles.body:
As we head into Week 3 of the fantasy basketball season, one early-season narrative continues. The injury list keeps getting longer. Ja Morant has a Grade 2 hamstring strain and will miss at least four weeks ; Anthony Edwards had knee surgery Thursday and could be out two months or more . Jaren Jackson Jr. tore his MCL and has a timeline of 6-8 weeks . Chet Holmgren has a small patellar tendon tear in his right knee, costing him 8-10 weeks . Kawhi Leonard (knee) is out 3-4 weeks and Tyrese Haliburton will miss at least two weeks with a hamstring injury too — all bad. Check out my injury roundup for more details .

Moving on to some good news: Coby White (calf) is off the injury report for Monday, and Brandon Ingram (Achilles) was assigned to the Clippers' G League affiliate Saturday. Let's get to the pickups!

Every league is different, so I'm focusing on players under 50% rostered on Yahoo.

One piece of general advice for this week: don't rush to make a streaming move before Wednesday. Tuesday has no games (Election Day in the United States), so you're unlikely to fit streamers into your lineup on Monday, and the best streaming nights come later in the week.

Shallow leagues (about 50% to 30% rostered)

Pelle Larsson – SG/SF, Miami Heat – (33% rostered)

Larsson is a good pickup for anyone in 9-cat leagues. He ranks 86th coming into Monday, averaging 11.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.2 steals with just 1.0 turnover in 29.5 minutes. His current shooting splits are a robust 49/40/89 with a TS% of 67. We'll see how long the Heat continue to start Klay Thompson. It's clear to anyone that Larsson is the better player currently. He should be rostered in far more leagues, especially with Miami playing four games this week, with two on lighter slates (Thursday and Sunday). Miami also has a Wednesday-Thursday back-to-back where vets could rest.

Zaccharie Risacher – SF, Dallas Mavericks – (36% rostered)

The former No. 1 overall pick of the 2024 NBA Draft looks like a completely different player in Dallas. Shoutout to Dusty May for giving him the minutes and role to prove what he can do. Risacher ranks sixth in total stocks this season, averaging 3.7 per game. The defensive numbers on top of the rebounds (6.0 per game) and scoring nearly 10 points a game in 30 minutes makes him a must-roster player. He's a top-60 player in 9-cat and top-90 in points leagues. Dallas has four games this week, but I would hold him for the foreseeable future if he's available on waivers.

Ja'Kobe Walter – SG/SF, Toronto Raptors – (39% rostered)

Walter has taken off since Kawhi Leonard (knee) went down. In the four games since, he's at 14.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 3.5 3s in about 31 minutes per contest. He's starting in place of Leonard and has been a top-50 player in 9-cat. Toronto only plays three games this week, but with Leonard set for a multi-week absence, Walter should be rostered in all formats, especially 9-cat.

Julian Champagnie – SF/PF, San Antonio Spurs – (31% rostered)

Tobias Harris' calf injury has boosted Champagnie's fantasy value. He's playing over 28 minutes a night and has emerged as one of the league's top 3-point specialists. His 3.3 3s per game rank ninth and his 3-point percentage ranks fifth in the NBA. His defense has been the real surprise. He's producing 1.2 steals with a block per game. Like the others, he's a must-roster for me ahead of Week 3 because San Antonio plays four games and Harris doesn't appear close to returning.

Collin Gillespie – PG, Phoenix Suns – (43% rostered)

Gillespie is a schedule add for those in leagues like High Score. Phoenix plays four times, including two of the lighter nights (Thursday and Saturday). His numbers aren't amazing, but he's the best playmaker on the roster outside of Devin Booker. He leads the Suns in assists despite coming off the bench and is sporting a very strong 19% usage rate. Gillespie is slightly better in points leagues than 9-cat, but it's close. He's averaging 9.0 points, 5.8 assists, 3.0 steals and 2.3 3s in 26.5 minutes. You don't have to worry about the turnovers and poor FG% in High Score, so add him if he's there.

Saddiq Bey – SF/PF, New Orleans Pelicans – (33% rostered)

Bey's last performance was his best of the season: 25 points on 9-of-13 shooting and 4 steals in 26 minutes off the bench Saturday against Atlanta. For the season, he's up to 15.2 per night, and though he hasn't surpassed 26 minutes, he remains a reliable reserve with their bench looking pretty thin from a scoring perspective. New Orleans plays four times. I prefer Bey in 9-cat where he's just inside the top-100 in per-game value.

Terrence Shannon Jr. – SG/SF, Minnesota Timberwolves – (29% rostered)

Minnesota picked up Shannon's team option Friday and with Edwards out, he'll have a steady role in the 'Wolves rotation. Despite coming off the bench and a couple of off nights in consecutive games, fantasy managers can expect scoring 3s with middling rebounds and assists in around 20 minutes a game. Minnesota plays four times this week, and his usage should stay around 18-20%, a healthy percentage for bench depth across formats.

Scoot Henderson – PG, Portland Trail Blazers – (16% rostered)

Henderson moved into the starting lineup Saturday at Utah and had 14 points, 3 rebounds and 3 steals in 31 minutes. It's a huge opportunity for the former No. 3 pick, who was buried on the depth chart before Morant's injury. In his first game without Morant, he went over 30 minutes; before that, he hadn't played more than 20 in any of his previous four games this season. If he continues to start, he needs to be rostered, especially in points leagues.

De'Anthony Melton – SG, Golden State Warriors – (31% rostered)

Golden State plays only three games this week, but two are on light nights — Thursday and Saturday. I'd pick Melton up around Wednesday to get those games. He had 21 points on 6-of-8 from 3 with 6 boards, 3 assists and 2 steals in 27 minutes of Sunday's win over the Clippers, but Stephen Curry rested, so don't count on that playing time continuing. Still, he's been a valuable bench piece on both ends and on a light slate, he'll give you some counting stats.

Nolan Traore – PG, Brooklyn Nets – (9% rostered)

Brooklyn exercised Traore's option Thursday, and with Mikel Brown Jr. (17% rostered) resting and Egor Dëmin (ankle) to be re-evaluated in one week, Traore is getting some run. On Sunday, he had 16 points with 4 3s and 6 dimes in 30 minutes versus Indy. The Nets play four games, with a Saturday-Sunday back-to-back to close out Week 3. Keep tabs on the injury report, but Brown is unlikely to suit up for at least one of that back-to-back set over the weekend.

Jordan Goodwin – PG/SG, Phoenix Suns – (4% rostered)

A deep cut, Goodwin is an option on Thursday and Saturday if you want to stream. He's providing a mix of stats across categories and with such low rostered status, he'll likely be there for those in 12+ team formats. So far this season, the combo guard is providing 8.8 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 2.3 3s and 1.8 steals in 21 minutes. He's a top-90 player in 9-cat right now, just saying.

Aday Mara, C, Oklahoma City Thunder (39% rostered)

Jusuf Nurkić, C, Utah Jazz (44% rostered)

Cam Spencer, PG/SG, Memphis Grizzlies (13% rostered)

Isaiah Stewart, PF/C, Memphis Grizzlies (10% rostered)

Keaton Wagler, SG, Los Angeles Clippers (35% rostered)

Daniss Jenkins, PG/SG, Detroit Pistons (17% rostered)

Obi Toppin, SF/PF, Indiana Pacers (24% rostered)

No games are scheduled on Tuesday because of Election Day. Thursday has the fewest games of the week with two: Orlando at Phoenix and Miami at Golden State. Saturday and Sunday (7 games) are the best alternative options for streaming this week. All of the other days are too packed to fit in a fringe roster-type player. Unless there's a significant injury or event, of course. Every team plays Monday, and 28 play Wednesday. That's why I wouldn't make streaming moves before Wednesday.

Phoenix, Orlando, Golden State and Miami: They're the only teams playing on Thursday, with a game on either Saturday or Sunday. If you need 3s on the light slates, Klay Thompson (10% rostered) is an option for deep leagues. For Golden State, I'd take a look at Brandon Williams (4%) and Gui Santos (12%). For the Suns, also look at Luke Kennard (2%) and Dillon Brooks (44%).

Four games (18): Atlanta, Boston, Brooklyn, Cleveland, Dallas, the Lakers, Miami, Milwaukee, Minnesota, New Orleans, Oklahoma City, Philadelphia, Phoenix, Portland, Sacramento, San Antonio, Utah and Washington.

Teams to avoid for streaming (barring notable injuries)

Three games, two of them on Monday and Wednesday: Charlotte, Chicago, Denver, Detroit, Houston, Indiana, the Clippers, Memphis, New York and Toronto.

articles.title: 16-year-old Dhinidhi Desinghu scripts history at Youth Olympics, becomes first Indian swimmer to win a medal
articles.summary: India's Dhinidhi Desinghu created history at the 2026 Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to win a medal at the
articles.body: India's Dhinidhi Desinghu created history at the 2026 Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to win a medal at the competition.The 16-year-old secured bronze in the women's 100m freestyle, clocking 56.27 seconds. Croatia's Ana Bobanovic won gold in 55.89 seconds, while New Zealand's Alyssa Lawson took silver in 56.13 seconds.The medal adds another milestone to Desinghu's growing swimming career. She had earlier become the first Indian female swimmer to reach a Youth Olympics final after finishing third-fastest overall in the heats with a time of 56.80 seconds.A promising swimmer with another medal opportunityHer coach, Nihar Ameen, praised her hard work and recent performances, highlighting that she had broken the national record three times this year."She has been working really hard. This year, she has broken the national record three times. She is in form. She has another shot at a medal in the 200m freestyle event. In fact, she has a better chance of winning another medal there," he said.Ameen also spoke about her mental strength and experience, having already competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics."Dhinidhi is mentally very tough. She has already competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics. We are very hopeful that she will win another medal at this Youth Olympics."Desinghu was the youngest member of India's contingent at the Paris Olympics. She is now looking to add another medal in the 200m freestyle at Dakar.Khushbu Darjada wins in judoThere was more good news for India in judo, as 15-year-old Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada won her women's 63kg round-of-16 bout against Guinea's Mamaissata Camara.Khushbu secured a 1-0 victory through a yuko, a minor scoring point awarded for an effective technique.Her opponent also received a minor penalty, known as a Shido, for a rule infringement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Gabby Williams' 30-point Game 7 heroics earn WNBA Finals MVP as Natalie Nakase makes surprising world's best player claim
articles.summary: Gabby Williams has given the Golden State Valkyries their first WNBA championship and finished the season with the Finals MVP award.
articles.body: Gabby Williams has given the Golden State Valkyries their first WNBA championship and finished the season with the Finals MVP award. Her outstanding performance in the championship series has earned her huge praise from head coach Natalie Nakase, who believes the award means more than the regular-season MVP. Nakase also explained why Williams deserves to be called the most valuable player in the world.Natalie Nakase says Gabby Williams deserves the world’s best player recognition after WNBA finals MVP winSpeaking after the championship win, Natalie Nakase made her feelings about Williams clear. The coach believes the Finals MVP award carries greater value because players must perform under pressure throughout the playoffs and survive difficult series before reaching the final stage.“To me, the MVP is the Finals MVP. That means you gotta play through the playoffs. You got to grind. You got to go through a seven-game series. Like, she’s the most valuable player in the world. Hands down. Good job, Gabby,” Nakase said, as shared on the Golden State Valkyries’ YouTube channel.Williams had to deliver against some of the strongest teams in the league before getting her hands on the trophy. Golden State first defeated the Dallas Wings 2-1 in the opening round, with Williams scoring 75 points across the three games.The next challenge was even bigger. The Valkyries faced the defending champions, the Las Vegas Aces, led by five-time MVP A’ja Wilson. However, Golden State won all three games to book its first WNBA Finals appearance. Williams scored 25, 20 and 16 points in those three games.The Atlanta Dream then pushed the Valkyries into a seven-game battle for the championship. Williams averaged 19.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.7 assists during the Finals, according to StatMuse statistics reported by Sportsnet.Gabby Williams delivers 30 points as Natalie Nakase’s Valkyries win first WNBA championshipThe biggest test arrived in Game 7 at Chase Center on October 31. Williams had only two points in the first half as Atlanta went into the break with a 30-24 lead. Rather than asking her star player to force difficult shots, Nakase told her to stay patient and trust the game.Williams followed that advice and completely changed the contest after halftime. She scored 28 points in the second half, including four three-pointers, and finished with 30 points, three rebounds, two assists, four blocks and two steals.The Valkyries won 68-63, securing their first championship in just their second season. Williams later spoke about the message that helped her turn things around.“Nat told me to stay patient. I trust her with my life,” Williams said after the game. “I stayed patient.”Her performance also earned praise from people outside the Valkyries. Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry congratulated her through an Instagram story, celebrating another championship for the Bay Area.Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg also compared Williams’ performance to Curry’s shooting display, pointing to the way she came alive after a quiet first half.The championship also added another title to Golden State’s collection. The Warriors had previously won NBA championships in 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2022, and the Valkyries have now brought a WNBA trophy to the same city.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Mike Washington Jr. among slew of good RB pickups to consider
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his waiver wire column, providing top pickups for fantasy football in Week 9.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

Lamar Jackson (thumb, potentially season-ending)

Tyler Huntley (toe, potentially headed to IR)

Willis was the featured quarterback in this space last week, even though I highlighted him more as a long-term option than a one-week streamer. That's because of a difficult matchup with the Patriots in Week 8, but Willis once again displayed his high floor with 15.6 fantasy points in the contest. It's good enough to make him the QB14 with only Monday Night Football remaining.

In his previous two outings, Willis finished as the QB4 in Week 7 and the QB13 in Week 5. His outlook is also becoming brighter thanks to the emergence of Miami's young skill position players like Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington, Chris Bell and Ollie Gordon II. Between his rushing upside, the improving talent around him and the schedule boost, Willis will be a streaming option every week and offers an intriguing ceiling against more generous opponents.

Kirk Cousins is 56% rostered but would be the No. 3 QB add behind Willis and Sam Darnold, if available.

Michael Penix Jr. vs. CIN (20% rostered)

Desperation streaming options (if starting)

The Raiders' backfield was one of the more stunning developments in Week 8, with Jeanty playing a season-low 40% of the snaps and only seeing five touches. Meanwhile, Washington played 60% of the time and led the way with 25 carries for 83 yards.

Jeanty still managed 73 scrimmage yards thanks to a 45-yard catch, but this is a terrible shift for his fantasy projections moving forward. After the game, Klint Kubiak suggested this was not a one-game punishment and instead a sign of things to come with their running back room.

Washington has been the top pickup in this column before, as Jeanty entered the season banged up and has looked efficient with his carries all season. The rookie is bringing more juice on the ground and Kubiak clearly wants to see if he can provide a spark there.

You won't find Washington on the waiver wire in any of my leagues, but if he's available in yours it's time to spend up and acquire him. It's possible this evolution continues with Washington earning the majority of the early-down carries and Jeanty making the bigger impact as a pass-cacher. That moves Jeanty down into the low-end RB2/high-end RB3 range and Washington not far behind.

Don't get too excited about Johnson's 128 receiving yards and a touchdown on five catches in Week 8. After all, he only played 19% of the snaps.

The real shock is that he's still available in over 80% of leagues. The fifth-round rookie has been a must-add in all formats for a while, as the high-upside backup behind Kenneth Walker III. The only difference after this week, is that Johnson might begin to provide some flex potential even with Walker healthy.

As we approach the midway point in the season, the recommended FAB bids will increase, especially when it's a player who's one injury away from stardom. Don't be timid when trying to add Johnson this week, he's one of the best stashes to have on your bench.

The Colts look like a team ready for the season to be over, which isn't a great sign after… (checks notes)... Week 8.

The trade rumors surrounding Jonathan Taylor have only intensified since I mentioned McGowan as a stash in last week's column. Taylor even seemed a little emotional on the sidelines in the loss to the Jaguars, perhaps recognizing that it might be his last time in a Colts' uniform.

We still have a week before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, but at this point I would be surprised if Taylor isn't on a new team by then. As long as Indy doesn't get a starting-caliber back as part of the return for JT, McGowan would be next man up to start — with DJ Giddens as the new change-of-pace option.

For as bad as the Colts offense has been lately, they still have one of the 10 best fantasy RB schedules in the second half of the season, so McGowan could be a sneaky fantasy RB3 down the stretch.

What is going on with the Buccaneers offense? After throwing just 11 times for 64 yards and a touchdown in Week 7, Baker Mayfield somehow topped that feat by only throwing three times on Sunday and failing to complete a single pass.

And yet, the Bucs won both games thanks to incredible efforts from their defense and rushing attack. Bucky Irving is posting some of the best stats of his career, while his backup Gainwell has been nearly as productive with 14 carries for 88 yards last week and 25 attempts for 140 yards in this game.

Despite limited touches early in the season, this is a nice reminder that Gainwell can be dangerous when called upon. We aren't going to see Tampa's recent commitment to the run continue to this degree, but it makes sense for their offense to lean on the ground game. The Bucs are another backfield with a top-10 fantasy schedule the rest of the way.

So, consider Gainwell a fantasy RB3 with a much higher ceiling if Irving were ever to miss time.

Black is a rookie backup I've been featuring in this column all season, encouraging managers to stash him away in case of a Christian McCaffrey injury.

The veteran did get banged up in their last game in Week 7 before the bye, but was fortunately able to return to the game in the second half. That led to increased usage for Black, who rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a score. It was his highest output since a 15-touch, 70-yard stat line in the opener.

McCaffrey downplayed the injury after the game and with the time off, I'd expect him back this week. CMC later confirmed he is dealing with a "mild" hamstring strain. However, it's clear Black is up to the challenge if his number is ever called.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last season isn't the worst idea in the world. Black should be rostered everywhere and would provide RB2 fantasy production with RB1 upside if McCaffrey were ever sidelined.

This is an extreme long shot, but Conner is a potential trade candidate who's sitting on IR in Arizona. I have the veteran stashed in several leagues, just in case the Cardinals send him to an RB-needy roster before the deadline. There's also the possibility that the recent string of injuries in the Cardinals' backfield (Jeremiyah Love, Bam Knight) leads to Conner being activated and put into the lineup.

Tyler Allgeier is 52% rostered but would be the No. 1 RB add, if available.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at BAL (26% rostered)

Brian Robinson Jr. vs. CIN (25% rostered)

Antonio Williams/Treylon Burks, Commanders

There isn't a breakout league-winning receiver on the waiver wire this week. Instead, it's filled with a variety of WR3/flex options. That's why you don't need to go wild with your offers and I certainly wouldn't use my No. 1 waiver priority on a wideout this time around.

With Terry McLaurin done for the season, Williams was a hot waiver-wire recommendation last week. Though he didn't blow the doors off with a big stat line, he posted his second consecutive game with over 50 receiving yards in the win over the Eagles. It was also the second straight outing where he led the receivers in snaps and routes run.

His teammate Burks is also intriguing as a flex play. He stepped up before the bye with four catches for 66 yards and came through again in this contest with three grabs for 81 yards. Burks has at least eight fantasy points in four of his last five appearances.

DeMario Douglas has always been a risky receiver to put in your fantasy lineup due to his low floor. We witnessed that occur in Week 7 when he only delivered three catches for 23 yards.

However, Douglas has posted at least 15 fantasy points in his other three outings over the last month, finishing as a top-10 WR each time. Touchdowns helped his cause, but he's come away with very respectable yardage totals in those games as well (65, 86, 76).

With A.J. Brown's uncertain injury timeline and Romeo Doubs still on IR, Douglas is stepping up for Drake Maye. Fantasy managers can continue to take advantage by starting him as a WR3/flex option with temporary upside.

Mitchell is the most difficult player to write about this week, given my undying hope that his talent will eventually turn him into a strong dynasty asset. Sadly, he was on the bench in most of my dynasty leagues during his seven-catch, 142-yard, one-touchdown eruption against the Raiders.

There's no denying Mitchell has the ability to produce in an NFL offense, the problem remains consistency. It's going to be incredibly tough to trust him in a Jets offense that has so many hands calling for the ball, including Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr., Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Braelon Allen and Breece Hall (when healthy and if he's not traded).

This week it was Cooper who was left with zero in the box score. The week before it was Wilson held to two receptions and 26 yards. That doesn't mean you can't add Mitchell and see how this plays out, but I wouldn't get my hopes up for him turning into a startable asset in redraft. He's more of a boom-or-bust one-week replacement in good matchups.

Jordyn Tyson is 51% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Makai Lemon is 58% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Tyson, if available.

Keenan Allen is 51% rostered but would be the No. 4 WR add behind Tyson, Lemon and Williams, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 53% rostered but would be the No. 5 WR add behind Tyson, Lemon, Williams and Allen, if available.

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Gesicki has scored a touchdown in six of his seven outings this season and currently sits as the TE6 in fantasy points per game with only MNF left to be played.

The concerns over his reduced targets the last couple weeks went away with a four-catch, 76-yard, one-score effort against the Titans on Sunday. He's now tied his career-high with six touchdowns and he's accomplished it in just seven games.

At this point, Gesicki has definitely done enough to warrant being rostered in most formats, but remains available in over 80% of leagues.

Even if you don't need a tight end start, Gesicki is in consideration as a flex option. Remember, he's mostly used as a third receiver out of the slot anyway. The Falcons are a plus matchup for both positions, so Gesicki has a good chance to keep this streak going in a potential shootout in Spain.

Quarterbacks: Justin Herbert, Jacoby Brissett, Aaron Rodgers

Running Backs: J.K. Dobbins, Jacory Croskey-Merrit, Emanuel Wilson

Wide Receivers: Chris Godwin Jr., Xavier Worthy, Romeo Doubs

Tight Ends: Mark Andrews, Juwan Johnson, Jake Ferguson

Jacoby Brissett has struggled this season and was eventually benched in Sunday's game. Whether he's replaced for the rest of season by Gardner Minshew or eventually Carson Beck, Brissett's time as the Cardinals starter is nearing its end. His only hope for a fantasy revival would come via trade.

Regardless of what the depth chart says in Denver, J.K. Dobbins has been overtaken by Jonah Coleman. The veteran has played less than 25% of the snaps in each of past two games and there are also rumors the Broncos could be in the mix to trade for a big-name running back like Jonathan Taylor. Even with RJ Harvey on IR, Dobbins can be dropped.

Godwin hasn't topped 50 yards this season and now the Buccaneers have decided to stop throwing the ball entirely. With Emeka Egbuka likely returning soon, Godwin can be safely sent to the waiver wire.

articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 9: Latest news, updates on Breece Hall, Jeremiyah Love, more players for fantasy football
articles.summary: We go over the NFL injury report going into Week 9, with player updates, news and fantasy football analysis.
articles.body:
Week 9 is the official midway point of the 2026 NFL season. So by now you know what you have on your fantasy football roster. You also know who has been healthy the majority of the year and which players have missed time. It feels like the injury report is thinning out a bit as we get into the middle of the campaign. But as always, we're tracking all the latest news and updates for you, to help with those fantasy football lineups.

Lamar Jackson, BAL (thumb) — Headed for injured reserve

Tyler Huntley, BAL (toe) — Could miss extended time

Ravens QBs : Jackson left in the first half of Sunday's loss to the Bills. He needs surgery on his thumb and is headed for IR . He'll miss at least four games, if not the rest of the season . After Jackson exited, Huntley entered the game and also had to leave due to injury (turf toe), leaving Baltimore down to third-string rookie Joe Fagnano. As if things couldn't get worse, Fagnano got banged up Sunday as well.

It doesn't look like Huntley will be ready for Week 9 and the Ravens can't proceed with Fagnano as the starter. The team is expected to make a move for a QB before the trade deadline, which is next week. Whoever ends up starting for the Ravens will need to be evaluated for fantasy. We'll update you when we get word on who the QB is and go from there.

Breece Hall, NYJ (quad) — Expected to be back in Week 9

Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Could be activated off IR

Jadarian Price, SEA (chest) — Expected to be activated off IR

Hall : We thought the Jets were going to get back Hall in Week 8 against the Raiders. That wasn't the case and we got another solid game from Braelon Allen. At this point, even if Hall comes back, expect Allen to be involved given how well he's performed. Allen is the RB5 overall in half-PPR scoring from Weeks 5-8 with Hall sidelined. We'll need to get a look at how the split is in Week 9 if Hall is back. Plus, it's a tough draw against Kansas City's run defense. But better matchups loom, so don't be surprised if both Hall and Allen are viable RB2/3 options.

Cardinals RBs : Love aggravated his ankle injury in the comeback win over Dallas in OT on Sunday. Knight exited after a big hit and should land in concussion protocol. It'll be tough for Knight to clear in time for Week 9 against the Seahawks, but we'll see. Love has had so many issues with the ankle in his rookie season, it's hard to view him as a sure thing for this week. If both are out, Tyler Allgeier will be playable, but don't expect 33.6 fantasy points — or anywhere close to that — against Seattle's top defense.

McCaffrey : CMC comes off the bye navigating a mild hamstring strain. It doesn't feel like this will cause him to miss Week 9 against the Raiders. But we saw before San Francisco's bye that Kyle Shanahan feels comfortable giving the ball to rookie Kaelon Black. We could see more of Black on Sunday to help keep McCaffrey fresh.

Emeka Egbuka, TB (foot) — Could play in Week 9

Jordyn Tyson, NO (hamstring) — Could come off IR

Watson : The Packers' lead receiver had a miraculous exit and return to TNF's win over the Panthers in Week 8. Watson finished with an 8-113-0 line on 10 targets, catching a few passes after coming back from the hospital. But Watson revealed he's dealing with a broken rib, which is less than ideal. He'll have ample time to rest before Week 9's matchup with the Patriots. Watson could play through the injury, but if he's active, he would be at risk of exiting the game early. If Watson ends up having to sit, Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams would likely see more targets. Matthew Golden would be elevated into WR1 territory as well.

Wilson : The Cardinals' receiver told reporters after Sunday's win over the Cowboys that he's dealing with broken ribs. It appears Wilson is going to play through the injury. He's a risky option in the flex in PPR formats going up against the Seahawks' stout defense in Week 9.

Egbuka : The Bucs wideout has missed the past two games, and Tampa's passing game sure could use him. The Bucs didn't complete a pass in Week 8's shutout win over the Falcons, instead opting to run the ball 56 times for 324 yards. That likely won't be the case in Chicago in Week 9. If Egbuka can get back, it's a decent matchup, though Tampa Bay ranks dead last in passing offense this season. Egbuka would be a risky flex at best.

Ferguson : The Cowboys lost Ferguson to a low-ankle sprain early in the game against Arizona. He didn't return and his status for Week 9 against the Colts could be up in the air. If Ferguson is out, this is still a passing game dominated by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Ryan Flournoy has stepped up as a solid WR3 as well. Brevyn Ford-Spann played 88% of the snaps in Week 8 and had four catches on five targets for 31 yards. In deeper formats, Ford-Spann isn't a bad streamer. He could see garbage-time looks if the Cowboys run away against a struggling Indy team.

Ricky Pearsall, WR, SF (knee) — Out for season

Jayden Higgins, WR, HOU (knee) — Out for season

articles.title: Pagani Huayra 70 Anima: una joya sobre ruedas con diamantes en la pintura y platino en la carrocería
articles.standfirst: Es el tercero y último de los Huayra 70, un hiperdeportivo único en el mundo con materiales propios de la alta joyería, seis salidas de escape y cambio manual de siete velocidades
articles.summary: Es el tercero y último de los Huayra 70, un hiperdeportivo único en el mundo con materiales propios de la alta joyería, seis salidas de escape y cambio manual de siete velocidades
articles.body: Pagani siempre ha cultivado el lujo y la exclusividad en sus coches deportivos. Pero esta vez la ha expresado de una forma diferente. Su última creación, el Huayra 70 Anima, no se conforma con una carrocería de fibra de carbono y un interior artesanal, como es habitual en los exclusivos coches italianos. Además, lleva polvo de diamante mezclado con la pintura y auténtico platino aplicado a mano sobre la carrocería. Casi más una joya que un coche. El espectacular hiperdeportivo creado por el argentino Horacio Pagani se ha presentado en el Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, donde ha compartido protagonismo con los otros dos integrantes de una familia muy especial: los Huayra 70, tres creaciones únicas realizadas para conmemorar el 70 cumpleaños del fundador de la marca. El Anima (cuyo nombre significa 'alma' en italiano) es el tercero y último de esta trilogía, formada también por los Trionfo y Derecho. Todos son fruto del programa Grandi Complicazioni, con el que Pagani lleva la personalización a un nivel difícil de encontrar incluso entre los fabricantes de coches más exclusivos del planeta. Tanto que son piezas únicas. Lo más sorprendente del Huayra 70 Anima está en su carrocería. Pagani ha combinado la fibra de carbono vista con dos tonalidades de azul creadas específicamente para este coche. Se denominan Azzurro Metallizzato Custom y Blu Inchiostrato Custom, que incorporan polvo de diamante para conseguir un brillo muy particular. Pero la cosa no acaba ahí. La franja principal que recorre la carrocería está realizada con láminas de platino aplicadas y trabajadas artesanalmente, mientras que una segunda línea combina ambos tonos de azul. Los detalles se extienden también a los retrovisores y las llantas, que presentan un acabado diamantado. Por supuesto, no todo es cuestión de lujo cuando se trata de un superdeportivo. El Anima tiene una estética espectacular, con abundantes elementos aerodinámicos de carbono, un enorme alerón posterior y seis salidas de escape, nada menos, rematadas con un revestimiento cerámico blanco. Y hasta en los lugares que normalmente permanecen ocultos hay detalles especiales. Algunos componentes mecánicos están anodizados en azul tricolor, mientras que los tirantes del chasis y los muelles de la suspensión incorporan un tono azul claro inspirado en Argentina, el país natal de Horacio Pagani. El habitáculo -siempre muy característicos en los Pagani- no se queda atrás. Se combina el cuero beige y color leche con tejidos exclusivos de Loro Piana, una de las firmas italianas más reconocidas del mundo del lujo. La fibra de carbono mantiene su protagonismo, ahora en tonalidades azules, mientras que el volante y el pomo del cambio también reciben ese acabado con polvo de diamante. Hay incluso detalles gráficos inspirados en las banderas de Argentina y Las Vegas. Sin embargo, entre tanto lujo hay un elemento que los aficionados a los coches deportivos agradecerán especialmente: una caja de cambios manual de siete velocidades, con su característica palanca y el mecanismo a la vista. Una solución poco habitual en un hiperdeportivo moderno (aunque muy cultivada por Pagani) y que refuerza el carácter especial de esta creación. El Anima mantiene la filosofía mecánica de los Huayra más exclusivos, con el V12 biturbo de origen Mercedes-AMG, aunque Pagani no ha comunicado una cifra oficial de potencia específica para esta unidad (los Huayra oscilan entre los 730 y los 900 CV). Detrás del Anima también hay una historia personal. Según explica Lorenzo Kerkoc, diseñador de Pagani, el equipo trabajó durante más de un año junto al propietario para trasladar sus recuerdos, gustos e imaginación a un automóvil. Todo comenzó con el sueño que aquel cliente tenía desde niño: crear algún día un coche especial junto a Horacio Pagani. Por eso, ahora que lo ha cumplido... el precio -que no ha sido comunicado- no habrá sido un obstáculo (aunque para el fabricante sí habrá sido una operación más que jugosa). Para su presentación en Las Vegas, Pagani reunió por primera vez a los tres Huayra 70 y los acompañó de otros 40 modelos excepcionales de la marca, en una celebración de la que difícilmente puede salir un garaje más exclusivo.

articles.title: HYROX star Joanna Wietrzyk beats Lauren Weeks in comeback race six weeks after Beijing controversy
articles.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk has returned to HYROX competition with a win in Hamburg, Germany, six weeks after a race in Beijing brought her worldwide attention after
articles.body: Joanna Wietrzyk has returned to HYROX competition with a win in Hamburg, Germany, six weeks after a race in Beijing brought her worldwide attention after a difficult six weeks. The 24-year-old Australian finished first in the opening event of the 2026–27 Elite 15 season on October 30, clocking 56:10.21. Her victory came after she faced heavy criticism for continuing to race after suffering bowel incontinence at the September race in China. Wietrzyk later admitted that decision was wrong, apologised to those affected and said the online abuse had taken a serious emotional toll.Joanna Wietrzyk beats Lauren Weeks to win HYROX Hamburg after six-week breakWietrzyk finished ahead of American athletes Lauren Weeks and Vivian Tafuto. Weeks took second in 56:24.37, while Tafuto came third in 57:55.34, according to the reported Hamburg results. The win marked Wietrzyk’s first appearance since the Beijing event and gave her a strong start to the new season.Her return followed weeks of public criticism. During the Beijing race in September, Wietrzyk suddenly lost control of her bowels but chose to stay on the course. Videos later showed her continuing through the event, with faecal matter visible on her legs and shared equipment. She crossed the finish line first, but later withdrew from the result and gave up the points she had earned.The decision raised concerns about hygiene and the safety of people using shared equipment. HYROX apologised for allowing the race to continue. Organisers said affected lanes were closed, equipment was taken away for cleaning and carpets were replaced overnight before the event resumed. HYROX also said people who sent threats or abuse to Wietrzyk could be banned from future races.Joanna Wietrzyk admits Beijing decision was wrong but speaks about online abuseBefore her return, Wietrzyk spoke to the BBC about what happened and accepted that she should have stopped racing. She said the problem began suddenly and that her focus as a competitive athlete had been on finishing the event. However, she recognised that continuing had put other people at risk.“Yes, I did make the wrong decision but I don't believe I should have received such backlash and such scrutiny online. At the end of the day I'm only human,” she told the BBC.She also said she regretted an Instagram post shared after the Beijing race. It included the lines “Go hard or go home” and “a win is a win”. She said she was in “fight or flight mode” while seeking hospital care and had not considered how the post would look.The athlete described the reaction as traumatic and said she had faced personal abuse. She also admitted that the experience made her consider leaving the sport. After stepping away from racing and social media, she said there was more to life than winning.Wietrzyk had said she was nervous before competing in Hamburg and did not want the Beijing incident to become her identity. Her coach, Chris Bayens, also asked people to separate fair criticism of the decision from personal attacks against her.HYROX has since updated its rules. Race directors can now remove an athlete if blood, vomit, urine or faeces create a health or contamination risk to that competitor or others. The change gives officials a clearer way to respond if a similar situation happens again.HYROX is an indoor fitness race that pairs eight one-kilometre runs with eight workout stations, including sled pushes, rowing and lunges. The sport began in Germany in 2017 and now holds events around the world.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald didn't commit to playing running back Jadarian Price against the Bears when he was asked about it on Saturday, but it looks like the rookie will be back in the lineup.

Price was activated from injured reserve on Monday afternoon and he had no injury designation for the game, so it would appear he'll be active for the first time since Week 3. Price has been sidelined by a chest injury.

The Seahawks could also welcome Zach Charbonnet back to the backfield on Monday night. He was activated in Week 7, but did not play in Seattle's win over the Chiefs.

Running back Robert Henry was waived to open a spot for Price, which leaves Emanuel Wilson, George Holani and Velus Jones to go with Price and Charbonnet.

The Seahawks also elevated wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr. and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed and left tackle Charles Cross have both been ruled out for the matchup with the Bears.

articles.title: Rangers Shake Up Defense As Durzi Sits With Undisclosed Injury
articles.summary: Sean Durzi's undisclosed injury forces a blue-line shakeup for the Rangers. See how Scott Morrow stepped in and what this means for the team.
articles.body:
The New York Rangers faced a sudden blue-line crisis on Sunday night when Sean Durzi sat out against the Edmonton Oilers. For the first time this season, head coach Mike Sullivan was compelled to rearrange his defense pairs due to Durzi's sidelining. The 28-year-old defenseman had played in all 14 previous games before this undisclosed injury forced him to the bench. Sullivan promoted Braden Schneider from the third pair to skate alongside Marcus Pettersson. This move left a gap that required a fresh face to fill the right side of the third pair.

Scott Morrow, who turned 24 on Sunday, made his season debut to fill the void left by Durzi. Despite the long wait, Morrow handled the pressure well during the 4-1 loss to the Oilers. He logged 15:02 of ice time and recorded an assist on the Rangers' lone goal. Morrow told The Post on Sunday morning that he felt ready for the moment. "Just view myself as being ready to go," Morrow said before the game, according to the New York Post . He also noted his physical state was strong despite the time spent watching from the press box.

"I'm in good physical condition and just excited to get in there," Morrow added to reporters. He expressed no frustration over his extended time on the bench, focusing instead on the organization's faith in him. "Just got to have patience and know that whenever an opportunity comes you just got to be ready to take advantage of it," he said. He handled the speed of the NHL in a losing effort.

In recent weeks, Coach Sullivan admitted that Durzi is dealing with a specific injury. The team has not labeled the injury as upper or lower body yet, which adds to the uncertainty. While blocking a shot during the 5-2 win over the Ducks, Durzi took a puck off the hand. That incident happened before the recent "maintenance days" that led to his absence. Through his first 14 games as a Ranger, the 28-year-old had collected two goals and three assists. With him out, the team must turn to younger players who have seen little game action this year.

Dylan Garand made 21 saves out of 24 shots during his 10th straight game in net. The rookie goalie has been a steady presence since relieving Igor Shesterkin following his season-ending injury. The Rangers achieved a season-high single-game faceoff win percentage of 64 against Edmonton. Will Cuylle and Luke Glendening led the way in the draw circle to help control the game flow. The team found success in other areas, while the defensive shakeup drew significant attention from fans. Durzi's health status is unclear, giving the coaching staff few options for the next matchup.

articles.title: PHOTOS: Fort Hill cruises at Homecoming, 42-3
articles.summary: CUMBERLAND — To win at Homecoming, you need to be near-perfect. Fort Hill was that — and then some. The Sentinels scored on six of their seven drives and pil...
articles.body:
CUMBERLAND — To win at Homecoming, you need to be near-perfect. Fort Hill was that — and then some.

The Sentinels scored on six of their seven drives and piled up over 300 yards of offense, taking down Allegany, 42-3, Saturday afternoon at Greenway Avenue Stadium.

"I'm really happy with our play," said Fort Hill head coach Zack Alkire. "Not that it was flawless, but we did everything that we needed to do to put ourselves in a position to win the game."

After winning the toss and electing to receive, the Campers (5-4) moved the chains with a Fort Hill (9-0) offside penalty for their first of nine first downs — Fort Hill doubled up Allegany's first down total with 18.

Two plays later, the Campers fumbled and Fort Hill's Melo Palmisano scooped and scored from 25 yards out. Bobby Brauer converted the first of his six point-after tries for an early 7-0 lead at 9:16.

"Everything we said we can't do, we did early," said Allegany head coach Bryan Hansel. "We can't fumble and give them seven (points) right off the jump. We talked all week that we can't give anything. They've got to take it from us. Now, don't get me wrong. They did take some things from us, absolutely. But we gave a lot early."

The Sentinels' next drive started at the Allegany 49 following a four-yard punt thanks in part to a huge bounce in Fort Hill's favor.

The Campers appeared to have the Sentinels stopped on the ensuing drive, but Levi House dropped a pass in the bucket to Jameson Powell-Morris for a 26-yard touchdown on third-and-13 to double Fort Hill's lead.

"He's a really confident kid," Alkire said of House, who took over at quarterback full time two weeks ago due to an injury to Brady O'Neal. "He's a very cerebral kid. So it's no surprise he's able to do what he's been able to do. A lot of respect for Levi to be able to come in and really play multiple positions for us on the offensive side of the ball."

A 27-yard punt return in the opening two minutes of the second quarter again gave the Sentinels good field position at the Allegany 33.

Four plays later, Carson Bender darted in from 21 yards out for a 21-0 lead at 8:26. Bender finished with 16 carries for 128 yards and a touchdown en route to being named most valuable player and voted offensive player of the game by area media outlets.

"He's really come a long way," Alkire said of Bender. "He's seeing the field a lot better. Probably most importantly, I'm gonna knock on wood here, but he's getting healthy.

"He has a lot of athletic ability, he has a great burst. He can see the field well. And now that he's able to really utilize that burst, great things are coming."

The Sentinels nabbed another third-and-long touchdown at 3:05 when House hit Neek Taylor for a 21-yard catch-and-run.

"We've had a habit of having big plays on third downs," Alkire said. "We put ourselves behind the chains more than what we like to the last three weeks. And almost every time now we've come away with some big plays to either score or get back to first-and-10."

Fort Hill had a chance to potentially open the second half with a running clock, but Allegany's Maddox Hensel intercepted a pass with 29 ticks to go to set the Campers up at the Fort Hill 30.

Dylan Blank ran 21 yards on first down to get Allegany inside the 10 for the first — and only — time of the day as Hansel called a timeout with 13 seconds on the clock.

Fort Hill got a quick jump on the snap on the ensuing play to force the Campers to throw it away.

After a delay-of-game penalty, Allegany's Landon Biser booted a 31-yard field goal to cut the Campers' halftime deficit to 25, 28-3.

Fort Hill's dominance continued in the third quarter, possessing the ball for 10 minutes and three seconds. Bender scored on a one-yard run at 9:35.

Taylor had the final score with a four-yard carry on the second play of the fourth quarter, which capped off a 14-play, 73-yard drive that lasted eight minutes and 33 seconds.

"I know everybody likes to see the big plays," Alkire said. "But from an offense that's looking to control the ball, and especially in that situation where you already have a lead and you're just trying to put away the game, that's exactly what you're looking for.

"You're looking for, I don't want to say three yards and a cloud of dust, but you want to be able to do what you can do to keep the chains moving and keep the ball in your hands. And we've done that two consecutive weeks now where we've had long drives in the third quarter to seal games for us."

Taylor was Fort Hill's second-leading rusher with 13 carries for 67 yards to go with an eight-yard catch.

The win caps off a Maryland record 22nd undefeated regular season for the Sentinels.

"We'll give the kids some time," Alkire said. "Monday and Tuesday, we'll probably bring them in, watch the game, eat some pizza and wings, do some fun things with them on Monday. Tuesday's Election Day, so we need to be off anyways. And then we'll get back to work on Wednesday."

Allegany's five-game win streak comes to a halt. The Campers have the No. 4 seed in the Class 1A West Region and will host Southern next week to open the playoffs.

"It gets tough to keep fighting, keep pushing," Hansel said.

"We never got in a groove. I thought we had some momentum running the football on some things, and then our motion's too deep, we can't get the handoff, things like that. … Our goal was to drive the ball long, hold the ball, and we didn't do that."

The Sentinels locked up the top seed in the region and the No. 1 overall seed in Class 1A, ensuring home playoff games through the state semifinals if they win out.

Fort Hill will have a bye next week before hosting the Allegany-Southern winner in the co-region final.

"It's always nice to be home," Alkire said.

"You've got potentially three games here. It's much better than having to go on the road. Greenway is a special place and we tend to do a lot of special things here, and hopefully that continues for the next three weeks."

articles.title: Why Steelers DC Patrick Graham Turns to Amy Winehouse After Bad Losses
articles.summary: The Steelers defensive coordinator opened up about a memorable bus ride following a difficult loss and how music helped him reflect.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham found an unexpected source of reflection after a difficult loss: Amy Winehouse.

Graham opened up about a turning point in his time with the Steelers, recalling a bus ride home from Cleveland when he spent the trip listening to the late singer and thinking about how he could improve.

"To be honest, I mean, I just sat there staring out the window listening to Amy Winehouse," Graham said, via 93.7 The Fan.

The defensive coordinator explained that listening to Winehouse has become something of a routine for him after disappointing losses. Her music matches his mood as he reflects on what went wrong and what he could have done differently.

"When we have a bad loss, I'm sitting there listening to Amy Winehouse," Graham said. "She's depressed on the song. I'm depressed that day."

Rather than simply move on from a difficult result, Graham uses those moments to evaluate himself and consider what needs to change.

"Just thinking about what I could do better," Graham said. "That was a turning point for me, and I'm glad it happened."

The Steelers hired Graham as their defensive coordinator ahead of the 2026 season. His comments offer a glimpse into how he approaches the challenges that come with leading Pittsburgh's defense and the importance he places on self-evaluation.

articles.title: NKU opens season with win in Field of 68 Opening Day Marathon
articles.summary: UTEP knocked down 14 of 24 free throws while the Norse made 30 of 33 in the Field of 68 Opening Day Marathon in Sioux Falls, S.D.
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. − The new-look UTEP basketball team had a quite familiar old problem in its opening 84-76 loss to Northern Kentucky: The Miners still lose games from the free-throw line.

Playing against a team that won 20 games last year as a member of the Horizon League, UTEP knocked down 14 of 24 free throws while the Norse made 30 of 33, wiping out a number of things UTEP did well in the Field of 68 Opening Day Marathon in Sioux Falls, S.D.

UTEP trailed most of the game, rarely by double figures, and was within 69-66 inside 4 minutes to go before a five-point NKU run proved more than the Miners could overcome. The Norse shot 50% to UTEP's 38% and the Miners made 8-of-30 3-pointers, as some other old problems of shooting arose. UTEP also struggled to contain NKU's guards, accounting for much of the 24 Miner fouls.

"We've got a starting point now," coach Joe Golding said. "There's plenty that we've got to get better at on both sides of the floor. Offensively we shoot 39% for the game, we let them shoot 50%, and then the free throw line they outscored us 16. We had 14 offensive boards and only got 10 points out of it.

"If I'm frustrated with anything, it's the toughness. We've got to get tougher on both sides of the ball. There is plenty of work work to do on the offensive and defensive ends. We have to get a lot better this week."

Freshman Willie Foster led NKU with 24 points and 10 rebounds and senior Noah Pagotto also had a double-double with 19 points and 12 rebounds.

Freshman Youssouf Traore led the Miners with 18 points and six rebounds, Donovan Criss added 13 points and Augusto Cassia had 10 points.

articles.title: Carson Hocevar Says He Was ‘Just Having Fun’ After Austin Cindric Martinsville Incident
articles.summary: Carson Hocevar has responded to his run-in with Austin Cindric at Martinsville, offering a very different perspective on the contact that ended Cindric's rac...
articles.body:
Austin Cindric wasn't laughing after his run-in with Carson Hocevar at Martinsville Speedway. Hocevar, however, had a considerably different interpretation of what happened.

The Spire Motorsports driver defended his actions following Sunday's NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500, insisting the contact that left Cindric with a badly damaged race car was simply part of short-track racing.

And despite the frustration coming from the Team Penske camp, Hocevar maintained that the two drivers were just having fun.

Carson Hocevar Responds to Austin Cindric Incident

The trouble unfolded just past the 200-lap mark as Cindric battled Hocevar for position. Cindric repeatedly made contact with the rear of Hocevar's No. 77 Chevrolet after Hocevar appeared to slow abruptly in front of him.

The resulting damage was extensive. Cindric's No. 2 Ford suffered significant front-end damage, ultimately forcing him out of the race and leaving him 36th in the finishing order. Hocevar continued and finished 21st.

Asked by NBC whether the contact was intentional, Hocevar rejected the suggestion.

"No, I don't know, I got lost there for a second," Hocevar initially said.

When pressed further, he offered a more detailed explanation.

"No, I mean, I got full throttled here in the spring and I just think it's Martinsville. I had a lot of fun and I think me and Austin have raced each other really well, or at least I've been pointed him by a lot – his cars have been really fast. So, no, I just think that's just Martinsville and I think we were just having fun."

Hocevar's explanation was a far cry from how Cindric viewed the incident, particularly given the damage it caused.

Austin Cindric Had a Much Different Reaction

Cindric made his frustration clear over the team radio as the contact unfolded.

"NASCAR, what are we doing? Like, we're just weaponizing cars here. I stack on entry with the guy and he has a mental breakdown," Cindric said.

The exchange also raised questions about whether Hocevar had deliberately slowed in front of Cindric. Onboard footage showed repeated braking as Cindric closed on the No. 77.

Hocevar continued to defend his driving during a subsequent media session, describing the contact as ordinary Martinsville racing rather than something personal.

"I just felt like it was normal Martinsville racing," he said. "Everybody's trying to move people."

He acknowledged that drivers were going to make contact while fighting for position, particularly on restarts at a track where passing rarely comes easily.

That explanation may not offer Cindric much comfort. His afternoon ended in the garage, while Hocevar was able to finish the race.

For Hocevar, it was another afternoon of aggressive short-track racing. For Cindric, it was a costly encounter that he clearly didn't find nearly as entertaining.

articles.title: Jaylon Johnson Owns His Mistakes While Critics Point Fingers
articles.summary: Bears CB Jaylon Johnson faces heat over a missed tackle but admits he must improve. See why his blunt self-criticism matters more than outside noise.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson is the only one who can fix his recent mistakes, and he knows it better than anyone else. Retired center Olin Kreutz posted on X, comparing Johnson's missed tackle to a teammate's fumble, and the cornerback said he would not make excuses. Johnson told the Chicago Tribune he must simply get the job done, acknowledging that his angles and pursuit need work after a costly play against the New England Patriots.

The trouble started in the second quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over New England on Thursday, Oct. 22. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye scrambled right, and Johnson peeled off his man to make the stop. Instead of bringing Maye down, the quarterback ducked inside and gained 15 yards. That single play has become the lightning rod for critics who question Johnson's effort and technique this season.

Kreutz didn't name Johnson directly, but his post drew a clear parallel to the fumble by D'Andre Swift in Week 4. "If you can go to the Bench (sic) for fumbling should be the same for tackling," Kreutz posted. Johnson responded with blunt honesty, telling the Tribune, "Yeah, I've just got to be better on those." He noted that keeping his technique in mind during open-field tackles is the only path forward.

This pressure is heavy because the Bears invested a massive four-year, $76 million contract extension in Johnson back in March 2024. He was coming off a career year where he made the Pro Bowl and earned second-team All-Pro honors. Now, his overall play hasn't reached that expected level, and head coach Ben Johnson admitted there have been ups and downs. The coach said the team evaluates every game to see who steps up and who warrants more playing time.

Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen offered a broader view, noting that every player has moments where they struggle. He reminded everyone that 11 guys are out there on the field together, and the defense works as a unit. Yet, for a player with Johnson's salary and reputation, the standard remains higher than just "good enough."

Johnson's own words suggest he understands the stakes better than the noise outside the building. He said there is no excuse based on logic or reason., adding that it is merely about angles, pursuit, and keeping technique in mind. As the team prepares to face the Seattle Seahawks on Monday, Nov. 2, at Lumen Field, the focus must shift from what critics say to what Johnson does.

articles.title: Michigan Could Get Two Major Reinforcements Back Just in Time for Michigan State
articles.summary: Kyle Whittingham says Michigan expects John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols to return against Michigan State in Saturday's rivalry showdown.
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines are preparing for Saturday night's rivalry showdown against Michigan State, and head coach Kyle Whittingham delivered some encouraging news Monday afternoon.

Two important defensive players are expected to return.

During his weekly press conference, Whittingham revealed that edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols are expected to play against the Spartans after missing Saturday's 28-21 victory over Rutgers.

For a Michigan team looking to build momentum and secure bowl eligibility, the potential return of two key defenders couldn't come at a much better time.

Kyle Whittingham Shares Encouraging Michigan Injury Update

When asked about the availability of Daley and Nichols, Whittingham provided a brief but encouraging response.

"Yeah, we expect them to play this week. That's what we expected," Whittingham said .

Neither player was available against Rutgers, forcing Michigan to rely on other contributors along its defensive front.

However, their expected return would give the Wolverines additional depth and experience heading into one of the most important games on their schedule.

Daley, in particular, has been one of Michigan's most productive defensive players this season.

According to Michigan's official Week 10 game notes , Daley leads the Wolverines with 6.5 tackles for loss and four sacks through eight games.

That's significant production for a defense that has already established itself as one of the nation's best.

Nichols, meanwhile, has been an important part of Michigan's edge rotation, providing another option for generating pressure and setting the edge against opposing rushing attacks.

While Whittingham expects both players to return, their availability has not yet been confirmed on the final game-day injury report.

Michigan Defense Could Become Even More Dangerous

Even without Daley and Nichols against Rutgers, Michigan's defense continued to produce impressive numbers.

The Wolverines held the Scarlet Knights to 249 total yards while recording a defensive touchdown that helped keep Michigan within striking distance before its fourth-quarter comeback.

Through eight games, Michigan ranks third nationally in total defense, allowing just 250 yards per contest. The Wolverines also rank fifth in passing defense, surrendering only 150.6 yards per game.

Adding Daley and Nichols back into that group could provide a significant boost to Michigan's ability to pressure the quarterback without relying on additional blitzers.

That could be particularly important against a Michigan State offense that has struggled throughout the 2026 season.

Wolverines Preparing for Saturday Night Rivalry

Michigan enters the rivalry matchup at 5-3 following Saturday's victory over Rutgers, while Michigan State sits at 2-6.

As we previously reported when the kickoff time was announced , the Wolverines and Spartans will square off Saturday, November 7, at 7:30 p.m. ET at Michigan Stadium.

Michigan has won four consecutive meetings in the series and will look to make it five while securing its sixth victory of the season.

The Wolverines also received clarity at quarterback Monday, when Whittingham confirmed that freshman Tommy Carr would remain his starter moving forward.

As we reported following that announcement , Carr has taken control of Michigan's offense after helping the Wolverines defeat Rutgers.

Now, with Daley and Nichols expected back, Michigan could be getting stronger on both sides of the football at exactly the right time.

And with the Paul Bunyan Trophy on the line Saturday night, the Wolverines will gladly welcome any additional firepower they can get.

articles.title: Fumble return 21 years in the making sets tone for Fort Hill defense
articles.summary: CUMBERLAND — The play that put Fort Hill on the scoreboard in Saturday’s Homecoming game was 21 years in the making. During the 2005 edition of the game, a F...
articles.body:
CUMBERLAND — The play that put Fort Hill on the scoreboard in Saturday's Homecoming game was 21 years in the making.

During the 2005 edition of the game, a Fort Hill player had an opportunity for a scoop-and-score, but couldn't pick it up in what ended up being a 21-14 win for Allegany.

The Campers routed the Sentinels 38-16 a week later in the West Region playoffs on their way to a 14-0 season and a Class 1A state title.

But in this year's game, Ramelo Palmisano returned a scoop-and-score in the opening three minutes to set the tone for the Sentinels' defense in a 42-3 thrashing of the Campers at Greenway Avenue Stadium.

On Allegany's fourth play from scrimmage, Fort Hill (9-0) blitzed and Harley Twigg forced the fumble before Palmisano took it 25 yards at the 9:16 mark of the opening quarter.

"It was a huge play," Fort Hill coach Zack Alkire said. "That play has been written since 2005. We had a kid in 2005 that could've picked up a fumble to beat Allegany in the Homecoming game and couldn't pick it up. So every year since then we've been practicing scoop-and-go, scoop-and-go, scoop-and go.

"Melo got the opportunity today to get a scoop-and-go down by the end zone, and it really set the tone for the game and got us going."

Fort Hill's stifling defense forced Allegany (5-4) to bring out its punting unit often. A couple of the Campers' punts were shanked, which often gave the Sentinels' offense great field position.

Fort Hill's offense went the entire first quarter without running a play in its own territory.

The Sentinels' first offensive play in their own territory didn't come until the 6:02 mark of the second quarter. By that point, Fort Hill was already up 21-0.

Even after the Campers intercepted a pass in Fort Hill territory with about 30 seconds left in the first half, the Sentinels limited them to a field goal to make it a 28-3 game at halftime.

Fort Hill's methodical run game kept the ball out of Allegany's hands and prevented any chance of a comeback in the second half.

The Sentinels owned the ball for more than 10 minutes in the third quarter, and triggered a running clock with Neek Taylor's touchdown run early in the fourth.

Fort Hill limited Allegany's run game to an average of 3.8 yards (113 total yards on 30 rushes). The Campers were without leading rusher Khiante Bible.

"Our defensive line is pretty dominant," sophomore quarterback/linebacker Levi House said. "All week, we've been working (on) run fit and just having our gaps and stuff like that. Our defensive backs ultimately shut down the passing game, so there was nowhere for them to go."

Sophomore Jaiden Beck led the Sentinels' defense with six tackles, including 1.5 tackles-for-loss.

Christian Riley was second with four tackles, which included one that went for a loss.

Owen Walker contributed 3.5 tackles, while House, AJ Adams and Marlee Williams each finished with three.

"I think it's just a tribute to our film watching and our preparation every week," senior running back/linebacker Carson Bender, who was named the game's MVP, said.

"It's every week we struggle with something the week before, we're great at it the next week.

"We watched a lot of film and we put work in throughout the week and it showed out today. We stopped pretty much everything they had for us on offense."

Like the 2005 Allegany team, Fort Hill controls its destiny after ending the regular season undefeated.

The Sentinels locked up the top spot in the region playoffs with last week's win over Smithsburg. They will have a first-round bye since there's only seven teams in the West Region.

But the Sentinels could very well meet up with Allegany again the region semifinals in a couple of weeks.

The Campers earned the No. 4 seed and are set to host No. 5 Southern Garrett in a quarterfinal matchup at Greenway next week.

"We don't like byes," Alkire said. "We would love to be playing this week. The guys want to play. It's just unfortunate that the system's set up for byes. But we'll make do.

"We'll spend some time together, have a little bit of fun on Monday and Tuesday and then get back to work on Wednesday."

articles.title: No time for Allegany to sulk after Homecoming defeat
articles.summary: CUMBERLAND — After another Homecoming defeat, there’s no time for Allegany to sulk. “I told the guys, ‘I’m showing up Monday, I’m going to work,’” Allegany h...
articles.body:
CUMBERLAND — After another Homecoming defeat, there's no time for Allegany to sulk.

"I told the guys, 'I'm showing up Monday, I'm going to work,'" Allegany head coach Bryan Hansel said following Saturday's 42-3 loss to Fort Hill. "We're going to be in the weight room, I'm going to go out on the practice field, I'm going to have a practice scheduled, we're going to go to work. And if you don't want to go to work, then it's like (the movie) Friday, you got fired on your day off.

"So if you don't want to go to work with me, I'll work with whoever wants to go to work. And I'm going to work, so please show up and go to work. If you don't want to, then you're fired and it's OK. Our goal is to go win a playoff game and see what happens after that."

The loss secured the No. 4 spot for the Campers in Class 1A West and a home playoff meeting with Southern.

It will be a rematch from Oct. 9 in Oakland, where Allegany won comfortably on the scoreboard, but not so comfortably on the field.

The Rams stayed in the contest through three quarters, closing a halftime 14-3 deficit to 14-9 by the end of the frame.

Following an Alex Spriggs interception late in the third, Khiante Bible scored the third of his five touchdowns less than a minute into the fourth and opened up a 58-21 romp.

On Saturday, Allegany won the coin toss and elected to receive.

After Maddox Hensel runs of four and two yards, the Campers had some early momentum when Fort Hill was called for encroachment to move the chains.

Hensel gained another yard on the next play, but the air was completely sucked out of the blue and white side of Greenway Avenue Stadium on the ensuing play when Fort Hill's Harley Twigg forced a fumble and Melo Palmisano scooped it up and returned it 25 yards for a score.

Things went from bad to worse on the ensuing drive when an errant punt from the Allegany 45 bounced near the Fort Hill 40 and took a Sentinel bounce, ultimately laying to rest at the Alco 49 for a four-yard punt.

The Sentinels capped off the ensuing drive with a touchdown on third-and-13.

They later scored on a third-and-8, and were 3 for 4 on third down on the day.

Allegany, meanwhile, was 0 for 6 on third down.

Trailing 28-0 with less than a minute to go in the opening half, Maddox Hensel gave the Campers some life when he intercepted a pass and returned it to the Fort Hill 30.

Allegany quarterback Dylan Blank rushed 21 yards on first down to get to the Fort Hill 9.

It was the only time the Campers got inside the 10 all day.

The Fort Hill pass rush forced Allegany to throw the ball away on first and goal.

With eight seconds left, the Allegany field goal unit trotted out on to the field for a 26-yard try, but the Campers were penalized for delay of game.

After moving back five yards, Landon Biser nailed a 31-yarder for Allegany's only points of the day on its sixth drive of the first half.

The Campers possessed the ball for only one minute and 57 seconds in the third quarter and had just two total second-half possessions.

The absence of Bible, whose finger injury two weeks ago against Keyser required surgery, was noticeable on both sides of the ball.

Offensively, the Campers ran for 113 yards on 30 carries.

Allegany entered Saturday on a five-game win streak and had rushing totals of 432, 489, 402, 470 and 328 during that stretch.

Over the previous five games before Homecoming, Bible ran for 173, 243, 278, 141 and 81 yards.

Bible was limited to just two rushing attempts last week against Northern — he ran Allegany's first play from scrimmage 79 yards for a score and then had the Campers' second touchdown on a two-yard carry.

Defensively, the Campers greatly missed their 2025 Defensive Player of the Year, as Fort Hill completed chunk play after chunk play.

Stopping fullback trap was a point of emphasis in Allegany's game plan, but it was unable to — Fort Hill fullback Carson Bender ran 16 times for 128 yards, with seven carries going at least nine yards.

Immediately after Bible's injury prognosis, the hope was that Homecoming was all he would miss, but he's in serious doubt to play against the Rams in the opening playoff round this week.

Hansel said Bible will revisit the doctor Thursday, with a lot of boxes that need to be checked before he can return to the field.

"That break was way worse than anyone realized," Hansel said. "So the doctor is going to check it and, if everything is set right, looks right, and the displacement is gone, then he could have a chance to get a cast and play next week or the following week. But there are a lot of boxes that need to be checked before that can happen.

"What I will say about Khiante is he is trying at all costs to play again this year. I can't fault him for trying. I think at a minimum, it's at least a burst of energy that we bring when he's out there.

"And I think it creates at least an option that you're forcing your opponent to focus on, and maybe opens up someone else to have success. I thought Maddox Hensel played very well in the backfield, but he can only do so much. We had to contribute more today."

articles.title: Week 10 Heisman Trophy power rankings: Darian Mensah, Malachi Toney close gap on Jeremiah Smith
articles.summary: The Heisman Trophy race had a major wrench thrown into it this season when Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an elbow injury that might end...
articles.body:
The Heisman Trophy race had a major wrench thrown into it this season when Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an elbow injury that might end his season. Sayin himself wasn't in the Heisman race, but star Buckeyes receiver Jeremiah Smith was leading the race entering Week 9.

The Buckeyes had two weeks to formulate a plan for what they were going to do without Sayin in the lineup and true freshman Luke Fahey under center. What Ryan Day and company came up with didn't work, as Smith had a relatively quiet night in the Southern California rain and Ohio State took its second loss of the season against USC.

Across the country on Saturday night, Miami survived another shootout on the road against North Carolina to keep the Hurricanes' No. 1 ranking. While the Miami defense continues to disappoint, the offense is still nearly unstoppable thanks to Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

As a result, Mensah and Toney keep rising up the Heisman Trophy power rankings and closing the gap on Smith. Which Miami star is getting closer, and who rounds out the top five? Let's get into the list.

Honorable mention: Notre Dame QB C.J. Carr, Oregon State WR Jesse Legree, Oklahoma State Drew Mestemaker, Utah QB Devon Dampier, Georgia QB Gunner Stockton

The fifth spot in these rankings has been up for grabs for a long time now, and Lopez gets the nod this week. Wake Forest is quietly one of the best stories in the country, as Jake Dickert has the Demon Deacons at 7-1 and ranked No. 14 in the AP poll. At the moment, Wake Forest has the inside track to the ACC Championship Game.

Lopez has been a big part of that, and he has a redemption arc of his own after being cast aside following a brutal 2025 season at North Carolina. On the season, he has completed more than 67% of his passes for 2,176 yards and 18 touchdowns to just one interception. On top of that, he has 317 yards and six touchdowns on the ground for a Wake Forest offense that ranks ninth in scoring offense and 16th in total offense in college football this year.

After a rough night against Texas, Chambliss was back to himself on Saturday in a 45-15 win over Auburn. In that game, the star signal-caller finished 22-of-34 with 263 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. He also carried the ball seven times for 65 yards and a score as the Rebels pulled away from Auburn's upset bid in the second half. Ole Miss still has to win out in order to keep its CFP hopes alive and keep Chambliss in the Heisman discussion, but doing so would take the kind of feat that could vault him into the top spot.

Ole Miss welcomes Georgia to Oxford next week, the same team Chambliss torched twice on his way to becoming a household name in college football last season. If he can do that again and beat Kirby Smart and company on Saturday, he will be right back in the conversation at the top of the Heisman rankings.

Toney made big play after big play on Saturday night for Miami against North Carolina, which is becoming his forte whenever the Hurricanes need him to come up with the goods. The star receiver finished with seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns and was Darian Mensah's top target once again.

On the season, Toney now ranks among the very best in the country on the stat sheet. He is currently third in receiving yards, second in receptions and second in touchdowns on the season. It might be hard for him to pass his quarterback on this list the way that he is playing, but this pace will get him a trip to New York in December.

Mensah continues to be just what Miami needs, when it needs it. He has been the best quarterback in college football so far this season and kept that up on Saturday, finishing 22-of-29 with 274 yards and three touchdowns while running for 36 yards on four carries. His efficiency continues to be the engine that drives this Hurricanes offense, and with the shaky defense on the other side, it is the main factor keeping Miami ranked No. 1 in the country. Mensah can make his case for No. 1 on Saturday against Notre Dame.

Smith had a quiet night narratively on Saturday night while Ohio State's offense sputtered in the loss to USC, but his final stats actually came out okay. The Heisman favorite finished the game with 10 catches for 83 yards and a touchdown. He is still fifth in the nation in catches, second in yards and second in touchdowns.

Ohio State's schedule is a little bit lighter at the end of the season, but they still play against a gauntlet of good defenses in Oregon, Northwestern and Michigan. It remains to be seen if Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair gets the start for the Buckeyes against Oregon on Saturday, but Smith is the key to Ohio State winning out and getting into the CFP. Even though it looks bleak after Saturday night, Smith is still good enough to get Ohio State to that level.
